name: JellyRock Companion
description: The server-side companion for the JellyRock Roku app. Cold-launch cast: cast from the Jellyfin web or mobile app to a Roku even when JellyRock is closed; the plugin lists the closed Roku as a "Play On" target and opens the item on it (http and https; JellyRock v2.24.0 or newer). Remote control on HTTPS: Roku cannot open a secure socket (wss://), so on an HTTPS server the plugin carries Play On casting and play, pause and seek from your phone to an open JellyRock (v2.23.0 or newer). Fast cleanup on HTTPS (v2.23.0 or newer): when you press Home on the Roku mid-video, the app cannot tell the server it stopped, so the session and its transcode linger for 5-10 minutes. The plugin detects the closed app within about a minute and stops it. On servers before Jellyfin 12.0 it also saves the resume point where you stopped, where Jellyfin alone would move it minutes ahead. On plain HTTP, remote control and cleanup need no plugin.
overview: Server-side companion for the JellyRock Roku app: cast to a closed Roku, Play On remote control on HTTPS servers, and fast cleanup when the app is closed during playback.

versions.changelog: when JellyRock closes on an HTTPS server, it now leaves its SyncPlay group, so the rest of the group no longer waits for it ([#33](https://github.com/jellyrock/jellyfin-plugin-jellyrock/pull/33)); on an HTTPS server, music and paused videos in JellyRock older than v2.23.0 are no longer stopped after about a minute ([#35](https://github.com/jellyrock/jellyfin-plugin-jellyrock/pull/35)); on an HTTPS server, closing JellyRock now clears its "now playing" within seconds, even when paused, and never stops a JellyRock that is still open ([#34](https://github.com/jellyrock/jellyfin-plugin-jellyrock/pull/34))

at-least-once command delivery via MessageId ack ([#10](https://github.com/jellyrock/jellyfin-plugin-jellyrock/pull/10)); Cold-launch cast producer: phantom session, pairing, validation ([#9](https://github.com/jellyrock/jellyfin-plugin-jellyrock/pull/9))
reap idle JellyRock playback sessions on HTTPS servers ([#7](https://github.com/jellyrock/jellyfin-plugin-jellyrock/pull/7))

Plugin catalog listing: clearer user-facing description, set the maintainer to Charles Ewert, and added the JellyRock icon. Documented that the plugin requires JellyRock v2.23.0 or newer (the release that added HTTPS remote-control support).

Release automation: push a `release-x.y.z` branch to bump the version, package the plugin with [jprm](https://github.com/oddstr13/jellyfin-plugin-repository-manager), publish a GitHub release, and refresh the plugin-repo `manifest.json` so the Jellyfin Dashboard can install and auto-update the plugin. ([#3](https://github.com/jellyrock/jellyfin-plugin-jellyrock/issues/3)); Install: the primary path is now the Jellyfin Dashboard plugin repository; the manual `scp`/`docker cp` sideload is kept as a developer note.
